content.title: HABITS THAT SOUND HEALTHY BUT ARE QUIETLY {{BACKFIRING}}
facts: **Chewing gum after meals** -> can make your stomach release acid as if food is coming, with nothing to digest, leaving you bloated.
**Taking a hot bath right before bed** -> feels relaxing, but if the water is too hot it raises core temperature and can delay deep sleep.
**Eating fruit as 'dessert' right after dinner** -> slows down digestion of the heavier meal and can cause gas, since fruit sugars ferment while they wait behind other food.
**Doing an intense workout on an empty stomach every morning** -> can push your body to break down muscle tissue for fuel instead of fat.
**Sleeping with your phone on airplane mode but right next to your pillow** -> the blue light from a glance at a notification still delays melatonin release.
**Drinking green tea on an empty stomach** -> the tannins can irritate the stomach lining and block iron absorption from your next meal.
**Napping for more than 45 minutes** -> pushes you into deep sleep, so waking up mid-cycle can leave you groggier than before the nap.
**Using mouthwash right after brushing** -> rinses away the concentrated fluoride your toothpaste just left behind, reducing its cavity protection.

content.caption:
A few of these are worth slowing down on. Chewing gum feels harmless, but your stomach can't tell the difference between 'real food coming' and 'just gum' — it still preps acid, which is why some people feel bloated an hour later for no obvious reason. Green tea is another sneaky one: those tannins that make it taste slightly bitter are great antioxidants, but on an empty stomach they bind to iron and can make it harder for your body to absorb it from breakfast. And that hot bath right before bed? Your body actually needs its core temperature to drop to signal sleep — a very hot bath right before lying down can delay that drop instead of helping it.
